sections.h2: What the Register of Deeds does
sections.html:
The register is responsible for the integrity, completeness, accuracy and safekeeping of every public record recorded in the office. For a house seller, that means the deed that moves title to the buyer and the deed of trust that secures a loan both live there.

The office offers more than land records. You can order certified copies of birth, death and marriage certificates online, where identity is verified through an online system and a vendor adds a small convenience fee. It is also a passport acceptance facility. Families settling an estate often need death certificates to support a deed or probate filing, and the same counter serves buyers, lenders and heirs.

Rowan County started electronic recording in August 2010 and accepts electronically submitted documents, maps included. It helps banks, title companies, law firms and other businesses in real estate deals.

E-recording offers these benefits:

  • No travel time or travel cost to reach the counter
  • No check writing, since fees are handled electronically
  • Document security
  • Real-time tracking of document status
  • A quick return of the recording information and a stamped image
  • An easy start for new users

An individual seller does not usually sign up for this. The closing attorney or title company handling your sale will already use a vendor from the county's vendor list.

Property Check emails or texts you when a filing appears under a name or parcel number you register. The register does not decide whether a document is genuine, so a fraudulent paper that meets statutory recording requirements and has the fees paid can still enter the record.

The service is free, runs around the clock and sends alerts through the contact method you pick. It can't block a bad filing, only warn you quickly. If you suspect fraud, call local law enforcement. Owners of vacant or inherited houses gain the most, because nobody is otherwise looking at the record. Questions on the system go to 704-216-8636. Register every name you have used on the title and every parcel number you own, and pick the contact method you actually check each day.

Have the Rowan County Review Officer sign the map first, then bring it to the register on one of three sizes: 18 by 24 inches, 21 by 30 inches or 24 by 36 inches. Review Officers work in the Planning Office and the Tax Assessor's office on the second floor at 402 N Main Street in Salisbury.

You get the original back after recording, and the office keeps a digital copy. Ask about electronic map recording. If your lot sits in a recorded subdivision or you hold a recorded survey, a copy costs $2 at the register's counter. Sellers sometimes order one to settle a boundary question before a buyer orders a survey. Bring the recorded map's book and page reference if you have it, and the counter staff can find the copy faster.

The state sets one fee schedule for every county, so these amounts apply in Rowan County as they do elsewhere, and the seller covers the excise tax.

Statutory charges at the Rowan County register
ChargeAmount
General instrument$26.00 up to 15 pages
Deed of trust or mortgage$64.00 up to 35 pages
Added pages$4.00 each
Cancellation or satisfactionNo fee
Excise tax$1.00 for each $500 or fractional part

The tax is collected up front, before recording. Half goes to the county general fund and half to the state, and a parcel that spans two counties is taxed in the county holding the greater value. The statute makes the recording fees complete and exclusive.

A conveyance, option or long lease has no force against lien creditors or purchasers for value until it reaches the public record of the county that holds the parcel. Time of registration sets the ranking between competing instruments.

Closing attorneys therefore hold funds until the deed is ready to go on the record. Ask yours to confirm that earlier mortgages were released and that any transfer from an heir or ex-spouse already appears in the Rowan County record. If a release or transfer is missing, fix it before the closing date, because the buyer's lender will not fund against a gap in the chain of title.

A death transfer starts with the court clerk, not the register. Plan on extra time for this step, because the buyer cannot close until the authority to sign is in order. When a small estate has no will, an heir may file an affidavit with the superior court clerk of the person's home county after waiting 30 days. The limit is $20,000 of personal property, or up to $30,000 when a surviving spouse is the sole heir, and the affidavit lists each tract of real property owned.

Estates above those limits need a personal representative named by the court. After that, the paper that shows who can sign the deed is what the register records, so ask a probate attorney before listing. A buyer's title insurer will want the right authority on record, and Property Check can watch the parcel while the house sits empty.

The Tax Assessor's office updates ownership for billing, and the register's office keeps the recorded image. The Tax Assessor page lists a separate land records contact, so a new owner who doesn't get a tax bill should reach out there. Rowan County Tax Administration also publishes a parcel map tool for checking boundaries and parcel numbers.

Recording is the moment the deed becomes public. After that, the real work is the tax proration at closing and any bill for the year that arrives in the buyer's name. The register and the assessor each handle half of the paper trail.

sections.h2: What to check at the register before listing
sections.html:
Pull the recorded deed that put the property in your name, then confirm that the names, the legal description and the parcel number match your sale contract. Rowan County offers an online document search for land records, so you can check this before you call anyone.

  • Search for the vesting deed and read the names exactly as recorded.
  • Look for each deed of trust and confirm a satisfaction was recorded after payoff.
  • Check for easements, rights of way or an old recorded map that affects the lot.
  • Sign up for Property Check if the house will sit empty during the sale.
  • Ask the attorney whether the deed will go in by e-recording or by hand.

Fix problems early. A gap such as a deed from a deceased owner or an unreleased lien can add weeks to a closing, and cash buyers value a clean record as much as any other buyer.

faqs.q: When did Rowan County start electronic recording?
faqs.a: The Rowan County Register of Deeds began electronic recording in August 2010, and the office accepts electronically submitted documents including maps.
Yes. You create an account, list a name or parcel number and choose how to be alerted when a filing is recorded.

faqs.q: Which map sizes can be recorded in Rowan County?
faqs.a: The register accepts 18 by 24, 21 by 30 and 24 by 36 inches. The Rowan County Review Officer must sign before the map goes to the register.

faqs.q: Who pays the excise tax on a Rowan County deed?
faqs.a: The seller, as transferor, pays it to the register before recording at $1.00 for each $500 or fractional part of the price.

faqs.q: How much does a copy of a recorded survey cost?
faqs.a: A copy of a recorded subdivision map or survey costs $2 at the Register of Deeds.
